newsitem.title: SPAIN: INSTANT VIEW - Spain cuts rates 50 bps, CPI flat. [CORRECTED 09:47 GMT]
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Spain cuts rates 50 bps, CPI flat. [CORRECTED 09:47 GMT]

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to Spain's seventh interest rate cut of the year and November inflation data.

The Bank of Spain lowered its key money rate by 50 basis points to 6.25 percent from 6.75 percent. Economists had predicted a reduction either today or at the next regular repo tender on Christmas eve.

In November, consumer prices were unchanged month-on-month for a year-on-year rise of 3.2 percent (corrects from 3.1 percent), after a rise of 0.1 percent in October for a 3.5 percent year-on-year rate.
-"CPI has developed better than expected. The Bank of Spain rate cut was to be expected with buying on the rumour when CPI came out and selling on the fact.

Both things are positive for the market. But later in the day the market will remain nervous expecting something from Dublin. But the Spanish fundamentals are good and the spread could fall at least toward 100 basis points."

- "CPI was good in general as was the core. It was better than the forecasts. This number allows us to close the year under 3.5/3.4 percent, which will allow the Bank of Spain to continue its policy of reducing the price of money. Both pieces of news are positive."
